messages: I've been out since last Tuesday and my inbox is a disaster. Go through email and Slack from then until now and tell me who's actually waiting on me, what they need, and when I said I'd get back to them. Merge duplicates across channels and link to the original messages. Don't send anything yet.

Can you check every commitment I made around the cedar-example launch over the last month? Look through my meeting notes, sent email, and messages with nora-example and dev-example. Compare those promises with the project tickets so you don't flag things I've already delivered, then give me a dated list of what's still outstanding, with overdue items first.

Friday catch-up time: review the waiting-on-me note in my knowledge base against this week's email and Teams messages. Close out anything that's resolved, add new promises I've made, and keep links to the evidence. Separate actual commitments from things where I just said I'd consider it, and show me what changed.

I owe a few customers replies but can't remember which ones. Check the last two weeks of threads involving harbor-example, birch-example, and lantern-example, including any internal Slack discussions where I volunteered to follow up. Draft a reply for each open obligation using the latest information in the thread, and flag anything you can't draft without an answer from me. Leave everything as drafts.

I've got 45 minutes before I log off for vacation. Find unanswered requests and unfinished promises from the past ten business days across my email and messages, then make me a realistic triage list: things I can finish now, things I should hand off, and things that can wait until I'm back on August 19. Check my calendar for deadlines, and draft handoff messages to the relevant teammates without sending them.
Is saying “I'll look into it” usually a promise to follow up, or just an acknowledgment?

Morning—check my calendar, task list, and unread work emails, then give me a realistic plan for today. I have to leave at 4:30, and the pricing proposal for cedar-example is the one thing that absolutely has to go out. Flag anything overdue, pick my top three priorities, and fit the rest around meetings with a proper lunch break. Don't move meetings or send anything.

I've got back-to-back calls tomorrow with mira-example at 9, the harbor-example team at 11, and devon-example at 2. Pull together what I need to prepare from our previous meeting notes and open tasks: what I promised, what they're waiting on, and any decisions I need from them. Put a short prep checklist under each call in my daily note, and set aside prep time in the free slots on my calendar.

My task list is a graveyard. Go through everything overdue or without a due date, check the related project notes for whether it's still relevant, and group it into do this week, waiting on someone, or probably drop. Merge obvious duplicates, but ask before deleting anything. For items blocked on other people, draft a follow-up with enough context that I can send it without digging around.

Help me salvage the rest of today. It's 1:15, I have a dentist appointment at 3:40 with a 25-minute drive, and I still owe the billing fix for juniper-example, feedback on ellis-example's draft, and my expense report. Check the repo, the draft comments, and the expense deadline to work out what's actually left and what's urgent. Update my task list with a doable plan, and draft any heads-up messages needed for work that won't fit.

Can you do my Friday wrap-up? Compare this week's calendar and meeting notes with my task list, catch any commitments I forgot to record, and mark things complete only where there's clear evidence they're done. Then make a Monday shortlist based on deadlines and dependencies, including prep for the northstar-example review on Tuesday. Save the wrap-up in my notes and show me anything that needs my judgment.
Should I prioritize an urgent task or an important one?

Meeting with nora-example at 2. Pull together a quick brief from my notes, calendar and email: who she is, why we’re talking, what we promised last time, and anything I still owe her. Put the urgent stuff first.

I need to reconnect with dev-example at harbor-example, but I can’t remember whether our last conversation ended well. Can you trace our email history and meeting notes, summarize where things stood, and draft a short catch-up email? Don’t send it. Also check whether he still works there before you write it.

There are two people named sam-example in my contacts and I’m not sure which one is on tomorrow’s investor call. Match the invite’s email address to the right person, then pull together their background and any previous contact we’ve had. Please keep the two people’s histories separate and flag anything you can’t confidently attribute.

I’m taking over the ridge-example account from lena-example and meeting their team Thursday. Go through the handoff folder, recent customer emails, and our call notes to map out who’s who, what each person cares about, and any unresolved commitments. Compare that with the invite so I know which attendees are new to us. I’d like a one-page prep note with links back to the sources, plus a few questions I should ask rather than pretending I know the answers.

Before I email ari-example about partnering again, help me figure out what changed since we last spoke. Find our last substantive exchange and the reason things stalled, then check public sources for recent changes at their company, meadow-example. Separate what we actually know from guesses, and suggest whether to reopen the old thread or start fresh. Save the summary with my existing notes on them so I don’t have to reconstruct this next time.
Someone I’m meeting lists “fractional CFO” in their bio. What does that mean?

The checkout tests started failing after the latest merge in cart-example. Run the failing tests, figure out what actually broke, and fix it without just loosening the assertions. Please also check that guest checkout and discount codes still work.

Our Python API on Cloud Run is randomly returning 500s when customers upload PDFs. One happened around 14:20 UTC today for tenant cedar-example; the logs mention 'I/O operation on closed file.' Can you trace that request through the logs and code, fix the underlying issue, and add a regression test? Don't deploy anything yet.

Can you look into why the nightly PostgreSQL import for harbor-example keeps creating duplicate invoices? There are two sample CSVs in fixtures/imports, and the scheduled job ran twice last night after a timeout. I need the retry bug fixed and a safe plan for cleaning up the existing duplicates—please don't delete production data.

The Android app crashes when I open a notification after logging out and back in as another account. Repro steps and a stack trace are in issues/284.md. Please reproduce it, track down where the old account state is sticking around, and make sure the fix doesn't break opening notifications when the app is completely closed.

Something's wrong with search on the atlas-example site since yesterday's release: results load locally, but production sits on a spinner forever. Start with the browser error and deployment logs, compare the production config with what's in the repo, and fix whatever is responsible. If it needs a production change, show me the exact change and how we'd roll it back before applying it.
What does 'connection refused' mean, and how is it different from a connection timeout?

Every weekday at 7:30 a.m. Eastern, check my calendar and put a morning brief in my inbox. For each external meeting, pull together the latest notes on the attendees and their companies, open action items from our last conversation, and any relevant emails from the past week. Skip canceled meetings and flag anything I promised to finish before the call. Start tomorrow.

Whenever a new invoice PDF lands in the shared drive’s Incoming Invoices folder, extract the vendor, invoice number, due date, and total, then compare it against the purchase-order spreadsheet. Add matching invoices to the payment tracker and move the PDFs into the right vendor folders. Put duplicates or mismatches in Needs Review and message me with the reason; don’t approve or pay anything.

Can you keep an eye on the CI runs for cedar-example? If main goes red, look at the failing logs, try to reproduce the failure locally, and open a PR if there's a small, clear fix. No merging or changing secrets. If it's a flaky test or you can't pin it down, file an issue with the evidence instead, and don't create another issue for the same failure every time it runs.

Friday afternoons, turn the week's customer conversations into a product feedback digest for the team at harbor-example. Look through the support inbox, call transcripts, and my meeting notes; group repeated requests, link back to the sources, and distinguish bugs from feature requests. Update the existing feedback tracker rather than making duplicate entries, then send me a draft digest to review before anyone else sees it. Use 3 p.m. London time.

I keep forgetting to follow up after investor meetings. When I mark a meeting with an investor as completed, check its notes for next steps, update that person's record, and draft a follow-up email with whatever materials I said I'd send. If the notes are missing, ask me for them instead of guessing. Remind me after two business days if the draft is still unsent, and stop reminding me once I've sent it.
Does a cron job run if my laptop is asleep?

The retry fix for orbit-example is ready on my current branch. Run the relevant tests and lint, check that I haven't accidentally included any secrets or debug logging, then commit it and open a draft PR against main. Include a short explanation of the bug and how we verified the fix. Don't touch the unrelated edits in docs/roadmap.md.

Can you get the CSV import changes ready for review? They're on feat/import-preview in ledger-example. Test both the happy path and malformed uploads, add a regression test if there's a gap, and bump the package's minor version since this adds a user-facing option. Update the changelog, push the branch, and open a PR with mira-example as reviewer. Please don't publish anything to npm.

I've finished the auth timeout patch in gateway-example, but it needs to go to release/2.8 rather than main. Check the release branch's contribution notes, run the appropriate checks, and make sure the patch doesn't pull in any of the newer auth API changes. Commit it with the right patch version and changelog entry, then put up a PR against release/2.8 with clear backport and rollback notes. Leave deployment alone.

Please finish preparing the PR for the accessibility updates in storefront-example. The changes are already committed on fix/checkout-focus; run the checkout browser tests and the usual CI checks locally, and fix any failures caused by this branch. Add before/after screenshots to the PR if you can capture them, describe the keyboard behavior we tested, and request review from devon-example. Check for an existing PR first so we don't create a duplicate.

The webhook deduplication change in relay-example is ready. Before putting it up for merge, test duplicate deliveries and retries against the local Postgres setup, review the migration for upgrade safety, and update the API notes if the response behavior changed. Create a clean commit, push it, and open a PR with the test results and any rollout concerns. If the migration could lose existing data, stop and tell me instead of rewriting it.
If a bug fix is backward-compatible, should its semantic version bump be patch or minor?

The settings page in this repo looks like six unrelated forms stacked together. Clean up the spacing, typography, and grouping so billing, profile, and notifications are easier to scan. Keep all the existing behavior, make sure it still works on a phone, and show me before-and-after screenshots.

We're starting a customer portal for harbor-example and need a small design system before everyone invents their own buttons. Use the existing logo and colors in /brand, and build a page showing type, colors, spacing, form fields, buttons, and alerts, including error and disabled states. It needs to work in light and dark mode and be something our React team can actually reuse.

Can you turn the notes in docs/checkout-feedback.md into three checkout mockups for meadow-example? People keep missing the delivery fee and thinking the order is already placed when they reach the review screen. Give me a few genuinely different layouts using the same sample order, include mobile versions, and recommend one with a short explanation.

Our analytics dashboard technically works but feels exhausting. Run the app and look at /reports with the seeded data, then improve the chart colors, number formatting, visual hierarchy, and empty/loading states. Don't change what any metric means. Check keyboard navigation and contrast too, and leave me a quick summary of what you changed.

I need the landing page for lantern-example ready for a demo tomorrow. The copy and images are already in this repo, but the current page looks like a generic template. Give it a more editorial feel with stronger typography and a clearer signup section, without adding a bunch of animation. Build the changes, check desktop and mobile in the browser, and fix any awkward wrapping or overflow you find.
What's the difference between padding and margin in CSS?

I've put my old Notion export in ~/Downloads/notion-archive.zip. Bring it into my knowledge base, keeping attachments and links between pages working. There's probably a lot of overlap with what's already there, so merge obvious duplicates without losing anything unique, and leave me a list of pages where you couldn't tell which version to keep.

Can you go through the Slack export in /data/old-team-chat and pull out the history of the harbor-example project? I care about decisions, why we made them, unresolved questions, and who owned what—not every status update. Add that to the existing project notes with dates and references back to the messages. Some plans got reversed later, so please don't present the early proposals as the final decision.

My dad gave me a drive dump of the family business, cedar-example, and it's a mess: scanned letters, contracts, spreadsheets, several folders called FINAL. It's under ~/Documents/business-archive. First show me what's in there and suggest what belongs in my knowledge base; wait for my approval before importing. Flag anything that looks like bank details, identity documents, or employee medical information so we can leave those out.

I have about 200 old meeting transcripts in /archives/customer-calls. Please use them to fill in the customer and contact notes, especially for mira-example at lantern-example and dev-example at orchard-example. Keep historical roles and preferences dated rather than treating them as current, link each added fact to its transcript, and put conflicting claims in a review list. Do a small batch first so I can check the result before you tackle the rest.

The Evernote export at ~/Downloads/old-notes.enex is my backlog of research, bookmarks, and half-written ideas from 2018–2023. Sort the useful material into my current knowledge base, preserve my original wording where it's an actual idea, and separate my comments from clipped articles. For bookmarks, check whether the links still work and retain whatever clipped text is available if they're dead. Keep a record of what you imported so I can give you another export next month without getting everything twice.
What's the difference between deduplicating old notes and merging them?

Review `feat/invite-expiry` against `main` before I merge it. This changes how team invitations expire in our Django app, and I'm especially worried about timezone handling and accepting the same invite twice. Trace the relevant callers, run the focused tests, and report concrete bugs with file/line references and severity. Don't edit anything.

Can you check whether `billing-v2-example` is safe to roll out? The branch replaces our Stripe webhook handler and adds a Postgres migration. Look at retries, duplicate events, and whether old app instances can still run while the migration is being deployed. Compare the implementation with the billing decisions in my notes from the meeting with mira-example, and flag any missing tests or rollout blockers. Please leave the branch untouched.

Give PR #184 a proper security review in the current repo. It's adding PDF uploads to the customer portal for cedar-example. Follow an upload all the way from the HTTP endpoint through storage and download permissions, including what happens with malformed files and user-controlled filenames. Check the dependency changes too, and separate confirmed issues from things that need clarification.

I'm taking over `perf/search-cache-example` from jonah-example and don't trust the benchmark numbers in the PR description yet. Compare it with the merge base, reproduce the claimed speedup if you can, and look for stale results, cross-tenant cache leaks, and memory growth. Run whatever local checks are reasonable, but don't hit production services. Tell me what should block merge versus what can wait.

Please review the React/TypeScript changes on `release/settings-redesign-example` before this afternoon's merge. Check the diff against the existing API contracts, exercise the changed settings screens locally, and pay particular attention to keyboard navigation, failed saves, and unsaved edits when switching accounts. There are acceptance criteria in `docs/settings-acceptance.md`; use those to identify gaps, not just lint errors. End with a merge recommendation and the specific checks you couldn't complete.
In a code review, what's the difference between a blocking comment and a nit?

Set up a personal knowledge base in ~/notes-example on this laptop. I want Markdown files I can edit in Obsidian, Git backups to my existing private GitHub repo notes-example, and local search that also works when I'm offline. Check what's already installed before adding anything, bring in the files from ~/Downloads/old-notes-example, and make sure none of those notes end up in a public repo. Leave me a short guide for adding notes and restoring a backup.

Can you upgrade the self-hosted SiYuan instance in ~/services/notebook-example? It's a few releases behind, and I have meeting notes in there that I really can't lose. Check compatibility with my Docker setup, back up the data and configuration, then do the upgrade and verify that login, search, and attachments still work. If anything looks broken, roll it back rather than leaving it half-upgraded.

My notes stopped syncing between this Mac and the WebDAV server sometime Tuesday. The local folder is ~/Documents/vault-example; there are now conflict copies of the mira-example meeting notes, and the phone still has edits that aren't on the laptop. Figure out what's failing and get sync working again without treating either side as the master and wiping out newer edits. Please preserve the conflicting versions until you've reconciled them, and tell me if you need me to do anything on the phone.

Search in my knowledge base is missing stuff I know is there. Searching for cedar-example returns two pages, but I've got months of notes about that customer, including PDFs and meeting transcripts. The app lives in ~/apps/knowledge-example. Track down whether this is an indexing, attachment extraction, or query problem, fix it, and test a few searches against actual source files. Don't send any document text to an external service.

Please clean up the mess in my atlas-example vault. I've got duplicate people pages like sam-example and Sam-example (2), old project pages still marked active, and a bunch of links pointing to renamed meeting notes. Start with an inventory and a backup, merge only duplicates you're confident about, and keep all unique text and attachments. Update links and the main index, but put uncertain merges in a review list instead of guessing.
What's the difference between a tag and a backlink in a personal knowledge base?

I'm meeting the founders of harbor-example on Thursday about their seed round. Pull together an investment brief from my notes and what's public: what they actually sell, who buys it, founder backgrounds, funding, and any credible evidence of traction. My notes from nina-example say they had 12 paying customers in March—don't present that as current unless there's newer support. Include sources, flag contradictions, and give me five questions worth asking.

Can we trust relay-example with customer support data? We're considering their hosted service, and I have a demo transcript and their security questionnaire somewhere in my notes. I need a vendor assessment that reconciles those promises with their current public security docs, subprocessors, retention terms, and incident history. Separate verified facts from marketing claims and unanswered questions. Finish with a short list of things procurement should request before we sign; don't contact anyone yet.

Need a competitive read on quarry-example before next week's planning session. Our product is spruce-example; the positioning notes and last quarter's battlecard should be in my knowledge base. What's changed in quarry-example's pricing, integrations, target customers, and product since that battlecard? Give me an updated comparison with links and a few concrete implications for our roadmap, not just a feature checklist. If pricing isn't public, say so rather than guessing.

I've got 20 minutes with dev-example, the COO at lantern-example, tomorrow. Make me a one-page account brief I can actually skim: what the company does, recent developments, likely operational priorities, and where our past conversations left off. Check my meeting notes and emails saved in the knowledge base against current web info, especially whether their European expansion is still happening. Suggest three conversation openers grounded in evidence, and keep anything private from my notes clearly separate from public facts.

Revisit my 'pass for now' memo on orbit-example from about six months ago. I remember worrying about customer concentration and a crowded market, but I don't remember how strong the evidence was. Has enough changed to justify taking another look? Use the old memo and related notes alongside current public information, show what changed versus what we merely learned later, and save a dated update next to the original without overwriting it. I want a clear recommendation with the biggest remaining unknowns.
What's the difference between a company's valuation and its annual revenue?

Turn my notes from yesterday’s launch into a LinkedIn post that sounds like me. The notes are in ~/notes/harbor-example-launch.md; look at my last 10 posts in ~/writing/linkedin/ before drafting. I want to talk about what went wrong with onboarding, not do a victory lap. Check any numbers against the launch report, then save two versions beside the notes: one around 150 words and one around 300. Don’t publish anything.

Can you draft my reply to mira-example in the latest email thread about the scope change for cedar-example? Read the whole thread and our meeting notes so I’m not agreeing to something we already ruled out. My sent emails should give you the tone—friendly, fairly blunt, no ‘hope this finds you well.’ I want to hold the original deadline but offer to drop the dashboard export. Leave it as a draft for me to review.

Newsletter time. Pull together this week’s issue for the founders on my list using the links and rough observations in my ‘weekly scraps’ notes, plus the product update for lantern-example. Read the last four issues to get my pacing and recurring sections right; I usually open with a small personal observation, not a summary of the news. Verify the claims in anything you link, cut topics I covered last week, and put the finished draft in ~/newsletter/next.md with a few subject line options.

I’ve got a messy essay draft at ~/writing/drafts/being-small.md and comments from dev-example in the adjacent file. Can you turn it into something I’d actually put my name on? Compare it with the finished essays in that folder, figure out which feedback strengthens the argument versus just makes it more generic, and revise accordingly. Keep my odd little examples where they work, flag anything that needs evidence, and leave me a short note explaining the big cuts.

Need a week of replies and short posts for the community around pebble-example. Start with the unanswered questions in our forum and the release notes from Friday, then look at my previous replies for how I explain technical stuff without sounding like support copy. Draft replies to the five threads where I can actually add something, plus three standalone posts—not five versions of the announcement. Check that the advice matches the current docs, include the thread URLs, and save it all in one review doc. Nothing goes live yet.
How do I make a post sound more like me without filling it with slang?

The README for parcel-example is pretty stale. Go through the repo and rewrite it so a new developer can get the app running locally, including Postgres setup, environment variables, migrations, and the test commands. Check the commands against what's actually in the project, and flag anything you can't verify. Please don't overwrite the deployment section; ops still uses that.

Can you document our FastAPI service's public endpoints? The code is in services/catalog-example, and the existing docs miss pagination, error responses, and which routes require auth. Add request/response examples based on the actual models and tests, and update the docs index so the API reference is easy to find. Don't put real tokens or customer data in the examples.

We need architecture notes for relay-example before the handoff to morgan-example next week. Trace how an incoming webhook gets from the HTTP handler through the queue to the worker and database, then write docs/architecture.md with a Mermaid diagram. Cover retry behavior, deduplication, and what happens when Redis is down; distinguish what the code actually guarantees from assumptions. Link it from the README.

Draft the release notes for v2.6.0 of ledger-example using the changes since v2.5.3 and any linked PR context you can access. Group them into new features, fixes, and breaking changes, and include concrete upgrade steps for changed config keys or database migrations. Leave out internal refactors unless users will notice them. Save the draft under docs/releases and give me a short list of anything that needs confirmation before we publish.

Our TypeScript SDK docs keep drifting from the implementation. Review the exported client in packages/client-example against the examples in docs/sdk, fix outdated method names and options, and add a getting-started page that covers initialization, retries, and handling errors. Make sure the example snippets type-check without making live API calls. Keep the existing docs layout and summarize any behavior that's currently undocumented or ambiguous.
What's the difference between a README and an API reference?

Move the staging API for cedar-example onto ECS Fargate. The app and Dockerfile are in this repo, and we already have an ECR repository and a Route 53 zone in the AWS account. Add the Terraform for an ALB, TLS, tasks, and the permissions it needs, then deploy and check that staging.cedar-example.com responds. Keep it to one small task for now and don't touch production.

Our GKE bill for harbor-example jumped last month. Check the billing breakdown and cluster usage, figure out what's driving the increase, and propose changes with estimated savings. You can apply safe changes in the dev cluster, but show me a plan before resizing anything in prod or deleting persistent disks.

Can you set up preview environments for pull requests in the lantern-example repo? We use GitHub Actions and an existing Kubernetes cluster; each PR needs its own namespace, app URL, and isolated Postgres data. Make sure closing a PR cleans everything up, secrets don't end up in logs, and test the whole thing with a draft PR.

We need to get the Azure setup for meadow-example under Terraform without breaking what's running. Inventory the resources in the staging resource group, add the configuration under infra/azure, and import the existing resources into state. Remote state should be locked down, and I want a clean plan with no resource replacements before we call this done.

The last deploy of orbit-example broke background jobs on our DigitalOcean Kubernetes cluster. Jobs sit pending, and I suspect the new node pool labels or resource requests. Compare the current deployment with the last working revision, check events and scheduling constraints, and fix staging first. Run a sample job through to completion, then give me the exact production change and rollback plan for approval.
What's the difference between a Kubernetes Deployment and a StatefulSet?

Can you click through the signup and first-run setup on http://localhost:3000 in a real browser? Try both a normal new account and a few dumb inputs like a blank name, malformed email, and passwords that don’t match. Follow it all the way to creating the first workspace in harbor-example. Report what breaks with steps to reproduce and screenshots; don’t change the code yet.

We just redid the cart for spruce-example and I’m worried we broke mobile checkout. Open the staging URL in the README, use the test account listed in .env.test, and run through adding products, changing quantities, applying the SPRING15 coupon, and checking out with the payment provider’s test card. Check desktop and a narrow phone viewport, including going back a step and refreshing. This is staging only—please don’t place anything on production.

The permissions UI in orbit-example looks fine to me, but customers keep saying it’s confusing or broken. Can you use the local app with the seeded owner, editor, and viewer accounts and actually test inviting someone, changing their role, and removing their access? Check what each account can still see after those changes, including with an old tab left open. Put any reproducible bugs in a markdown report with expected versus actual behavior.

Please do a browser regression pass on the search/filter page we changed in this branch. Start the app if needed. For meadow-example, try combining filters, clearing them, sorting, paging through results, and opening a result then using Back; also check whether a copied URL restores the same search in a new tab. If you find a clear regression caused by this branch, fix it and retest the affected paths. Keep unrelated cleanup out of the diff.

Before tomorrow’s demo, check the file-import experience in ledger-example at http://localhost:5173. There are CSV fixtures under test-data/imports—try the valid one, the duplicate rows, and the malformed headers through the actual upload screen. Make sure progress, errors, retry, and the final records table make sense, and refresh after an import to see whether the data really stuck. I’d like a short list of demo blockers versus minor annoyances, with screenshots of anything broken. Don’t delete the existing demo records.
What’s the difference between testing a site in a real browser and just checking its HTTP responses?

Add cursor pagination to the GET /events endpoint in this repo. It’s a FastAPI service on Postgres, and clients currently get everything in one response. Keep existing filters working, make the ordering stable when timestamps match, and add tests for paging through results without duplicates or gaps. Don’t break clients that still use the old response shape.

We keep getting duplicate payment notifications from our webhook handler for cedar-example. Can you trace how incoming events get stored and processed, then make retries safe even if two copies arrive at once? There’s a Docker Compose setup for local testing. Add a regression test, and flag any migration or deployment ordering we’ll need before this goes live.

I need a backend design for a bulk CSV import endpoint for harbor-example. Uploads can be around 2 GB, processing takes several minutes, and users need progress plus a downloadable list of bad rows. Look through our existing service and infrastructure config, compare a couple of practical approaches, and write up a recommendation with the API contract, failure handling, and a staged implementation plan. Don’t start changing application code yet.

Our staging search endpoint went from about 200 ms to 3 seconds after yesterday’s release. Check the recent changes and whatever logs and query plans you can get with the configured staging credentials, find the bottleneck, and put together a fix with a repeatable performance test. Please don’t change staging data or deploy anything; I want the before/after evidence and a patch I can review.

Finish the API key support we started for orbit-example. Users should be able to create named keys, list them without seeing the secret again, and revoke them; keys need scopes and must never end up in logs. Check the existing auth conventions before wiring this in, add tests for cross-account access and revoked keys, and update the OpenAPI docs with usable request examples. If anything about the current schema makes this unsafe, tell me before changing it.
When should an API return 401 instead of 403?

Check this Next.js repo for security issues before we ship checkout for cartwheel-example. Look at the API routes, auth checks, webhook verification, and anywhere we handle payment or customer data. Make fixes on a branch, add regression tests where practical, and give me a short list of anything you couldn't safely resolve. Don't touch production or use real customer records.

We've ignored dependency alerts in ledger-example for a while. Can you go through the Python and npm dependencies, figure out which advisories actually affect us, and update the vulnerable stuff without breaking the app? Run the tests and flag any upgrades that need code changes or introduce compatibility risks. I'd rather see an explicit exception with a reason than a forced major-version bump.

Audit our AWS staging account using the configured read-only profile staging-example. I'm worried about public S3 buckets, overly broad IAM permissions, exposed databases, and security groups left open after debugging. Cross-check what you find against the Terraform in infra/, then write up prioritized fixes with the affected resource IDs. Don't change cloud resources; prepare Terraform changes separately for review.

I accidentally committed a token to the harbor-example repo last week and deleted it in the next commit. Check the full git history and current CI config for that token and any other exposed credentials, without printing secret values in your output. Tell me what needs revoking, prepare cleanup changes, and add a check to catch future leaks. Don't rewrite shared history or rotate anything until I approve.

We added file uploads and URL previews to the Django service in dispatch-example, and I'd like a security pass before enabling them for everyone. Trace both features from the endpoints through storage and background jobs, then test whether an ordinary user can read someone else's uploads, upload dangerous content, or make the preview worker reach internal services. Use local fixtures only, no external targets. Fix confirmed issues and leave tests that demonstrate the protections.
Does a package-lock.json file guarantee that my npm dependencies are free of known vulnerabilities?

Pull together everything in my notes about usage-based pricing. Include the customer calls, the stuff I clipped from the web, and the arguments in the billing repo docs.
